rule: A vertical two-column legend of (key | value) rows sits on a uniform background. Each key colour appears either as two L-shaped corner pieces at opposite corners of a rectangle, or as a solid 2x2 block. On a non-zero background, value 0 means: first erase that key's pieces to background, and claim no rectangle. The remaining rows are applied top to bottom, and a cell is claimed only once (the first row wins). If the value equals the background, the rectangle's free background cells are reserved and left unchanged. Otherwise those free cells are filled with the value. A solid block has no free cells, so the block itself is recoloured. Non-key pieces and absent keys have no effect.
scope: Ordered key/value legend fills rectangles specified by L-corner pairs or recolours solid2x2 blocks. All erasures occur before claims, background-valued rows reserve cells, earlier claims take precedence, and key locations are read from the original input. Native scenes exercise legend order, reservation or erase-first; optional require_erase_first control retains its requirement across retries. All six canonical examples reconstruct exactly.

Erase rows do not intersect later claiming rectangles in native scenes; this follows the prior documented scope rather than inferring unsupported conventions.
Area-order alternatives are measured, not universally excluded: individual scenes can match ascending or descending area order. Forced erase-first scenes may have no order-sensitive fill overlap.

authored_scope: Random scenes: grids are 10..24 per side by default, and 10..30 when given explicitly (sizes above 19 are a synthetic extension). The background is random. The legend has 2..5 rows and is usually at an edge; mid-grid placement is a synthetic extension. Scenes mix fill, reserve and erase rows and both corner orientations, sampled per row and per pair. A scene may also include an optional solid block (always a fill row), an absent key, and a non-key distractor pair. Different objects may touch diagonally but never orthogonally. Every scene has load-bearing order or reserve semantics, and usually cannot be explained by sorting rows by area. Not supported in random mode: a pair with no free cells being recoloured; reserve or erase rows on blocks; erase-row rectangles intersecting a later claiming rectangle; rectangles that cover the legend; more than one object per colour. Explicit mode reconstructs all six canonical fixtures and renders the unverified cases using the same semantics.
authored_constraints: Legend keys are distinct, differ from the background, and at least one present key has a fill value. This keeps the value column non-background, so the legend bounding box is 2 columns wide.
Object rectangles never intersect the legend zone (the legend expanded by one cell), so objects never touch the legend.
Different objects never overlap and are never 4-adjacent. Diagonal contact is allowed.
No non-legend 8-connected cluster has two or more colours and a 2-column bounding box, so it cannot be confused with the legend.
The two pieces of one pair are not 8-adjacent.
The background is strictly the most frequent input colour.
Output differs from input. No corner pair is left without free cells.
Reversing the legend, or dropping its reserve rows, changes the output.
In the first 400 attempts, the output also differs from a randomly chosen ascending or descending area order.
An erase row's rectangle never intersects the rectangle of a later fill or reserve row.
Width, height, bg, legend entries, legend_pos and object fields must be true integers, not booleans; otherwise ValueError is raised. Partial explicit specification raises ValueError.
